body:
When the gateway resolves an entity lookup, `FetchResultStore` builds one set of variables per parent entity. Every set repeated the variables forwarded from the request, so the forwarded values were serialized from their syntax nodes again for each entity, including escaping strings and formatting numbers.

This PR writes the forwarded variables once per fetch and copies their bytes into each entity's variables through a new internal `JsonWriter.WriteRawProperties`. A fetch for a single entity still writes them directly, because there is nothing to reuse. The buffer stays on the pooled store and is released when a large input makes it grow beyond 16 KB.

## Benchmarks

| Entities | Forwarded variables | Version | Mean | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | None | `main` | 165.5 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | None | PR | 170.6 ns | 1.03 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | Few | `main` | 226.9 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | Few | PR | 221.6 ns | 0.98 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | Many | `main` | 588.0 ns | 1.00 | 192 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | Many | PR | 595.2 ns | 1.01 | 192 B | 1.00 |
| 25 | None | `main` | 2.912 μs | 1.00 | 1.06 KB | 1.00 |
| 25 | None | PR | 2.530 μs | 0.87 | 1.06 KB | 1.00 |
| 25 | Few | `main` | 4.146 μs | 1.00 | 1.06 KB | 1.00 |
| 25 | Few | PR | 3.586 μs | 0.86 | 1.06 KB | 1.00 |
| 25 | Many | `main` | 13.17 μs | 1.00 | 2.63 KB | 1.00 |
| 25 | Many | PR | 5.810 μs | 0.44 | 1.13 KB | 0.43 |
| 100 | None | `main` | 11.83 μs | 1.00 | 3.99 KB | 1.00 |
| 100 | None | PR | 12.10 μs | 1.02 | 3.99 KB | 1.00 |
| 100 | Few | `main` | 17.90 μs | 1.00 | 3.99 KB | 1.00 |
| 100 | Few | PR | 15.31 μs | 0.86 | 3.99 KB | 1.00 |
| 100 | Many | `main` | 54.84 μs | 1.00 | 10.24 KB | 1.00 |
| 100 | Many | PR | 21.65 μs | 0.39 | 4.05 KB | 0.40 |

This is a net improvement. A lookup of 25 or 100 entities that forwards several variables is 2.3x to 2.5x faster and allocates 60% less, and with a single forwarded variable it is 14% faster, because the forwarded variables are serialized once per fetch instead of once per entity. A lookup of a single entity keeps the direct write and is within noise of `main`. The `None` cases do not touch the changed code, and their differences are run-to-run noise, which is wide for the 25 and 100 entity cases. The costs are one 4 KB pooled buffer per store and one more write path in `FetchResultStore`, which are small next to the gain on exactly the fetch shape that batching produces.
